stem.en: Why do both lupus and systemic sclerosis typically affect multiple organ systems rather than just one, even though they arise from the same broken self-tolerance mechanism that underlies autoimmune disease generally?
stem.et: Miks mõjutavad nii luupus kui süsteemne skleroos tavaliselt mitut organsüsteemi, mitte ainult ühte, ehkki need tekivad samast katkenud enesetolerantsi mehhanismist, mis on aluseks autoimmuunhaigusele üldiselt?

label.en: Because each disease's specific immune target — nuclear antigens in lupus, connective tissue and vasculature in systemic sclerosis — is present throughout nearly every organ system, so the resulting damage isn't confined to a single organ.
label.et: Sest iga haiguse konkreetne immuunsihtmärk — tuuma antigeenid luupuse korral, sidekude ja veresoonkond süsteemse skleroosi korral — esineb peaaegu igas organsüsteemis, mistõttu tekkiv kahjustus ei ole piiratud ühe organiga.

label.en: Because lupus is fundamentally a skin disease that happens to occasionally spread to other organs in unusual cases.
label.et: Sest luupus on põhimõtteliselt nahahaigus, mis erandjuhtudel juhtumisi levib teistesse organitesse.

label.en: They don't — systemic sclerosis is primarily a cosmetic skin condition, and only lupus meaningfully affects internal organs.
label.et: See ei vasta tõele — süsteemne skleroos on peamiselt kosmeetiline nahaseisund ning ainult luupus mõjutab oluliselt siseorganeid.

label.en: Because both diseases destroy tissue through the identical immune-complex-deposition mechanism, which happens to reach many organs at once.
label.et: Sest mõlemad haigused hävitavad kude identse immuunkompleksi sadenemise mehhanismi kaudu, mis juhtumisi jõuab paljudesse organitesse korraga.
